collections.description: Jerry lost his brother Evan when he was only a child. The world wants him to believe that Evan died in a natural disaster. Jerry knows better. He knows his brother was taken from him, and he will stop at nothing to uncover the truth. This quest will put him in conflict with some of the greatest powers in the anomalous world and force him to question whether he can trust the people closest to him.

primaryArticles.title: The Global Occult Coalition
primaryArticles.desc: Group of Interest created by Kain Pathos Crow in the early days of the SCP Foundation wiki. Inspired by a creepypasta about how the Soviet Red Army killed God in the 1950s, it postulated the existence of a separate, but equally powerful, force in the paranormal world. If the SCP Foundation was dedicated to finding, capturing, and containing paranormal objects, the Coalition would be dedicated to a much different, more direct approach: outright destruction of the paranormal.

collections.description: The Department of Colour (DoCO) is a specialised division that studies and maintains anomalies and phenomena related to the electromagnetic spectrum, chromatic phenomena, and darkness. The Department of Colour is also responsible for selecting the appropriate colours for various Foundation items (uniforms, classification labeling, etc). Together, these various colours form a sacred colourology uniquely obsessed with protecting the Foundation. These charms are not immutable and are preventative in nature.

primaryArticles.title: Unsinkable
primaryArticles.desc: The ship is sinking. It didn't make sense, but then, nothing did. Her head was swimming, and so was the rest of her. Limbs numb, fingers senseless, she was breathing water as much as air. She couldn't tell which way was up and which was down; she only knew sid…

primaryArticles.title: 1. Hachiro
primaryArticles.desc: When the past is more than prelude, and you live it every hour, The milk of human kindness curdles into something sour, You grow complacent with suspicion's cry, so shrill and feral, And miss the warning wailings of the present, to your peril

primaryArticles.title: 2. Pilar
primaryArticles.desc: For the essence of a dug-out isn't made with pick and shovel There's factors in its form that wouldn't suit a homely hovel Underneath the earth you know the difference in a second The sickly stench of vigilance, though staler than you reckoned

primaryArticles.title: 3. Imrich
primaryArticles.desc: When you're counting down the seconds and each second counts for less, And the products of division are a source of some distress, Try not to let that mental math turn prophet into mourner, Who blinded by his tears predicts himself into a corner

primaryArticles.title: 4. Rasmus
primaryArticles.desc: But even up and at 'em far above your cozy shelter The guns are blazing fiercely and your wits go helter-skelter There's no man in that land to fight, don't trust you're apt to win it You've left your bivvy open, and your enemy's within it

primaryArticles.title: 5. Wynn
primaryArticles.desc: When your hat and boots are drying by the fire at the door, And you're cooking up a mystery mash with seasoning and more, Give thanks for all the earth they moved and for the roof they raised, The digging of a dug-out is a feat that must be praised.

primaryArticles.title: 6. Randolph
primaryArticles.desc: Some are spacious, some are homely, some are just a little strange, But the one thing that they never are is proof against all change Sappers, storms and ordnance must each extract a toll So be sure to keep your feet when next you pop out for a stroll.

primaryArticles.title: 7. Clio
primaryArticles.desc: When your codebook's out of order and your radio's just out, In static darkness silently you stew within your doubt You learn a truth no fractured pseudo-sanity can soften: A dug-out you can't leave is just a shallow-buried coffin.

primaryArticles.title: 8. Gabrielle
primaryArticles.desc: But though the fun on offer there may be a mite unvaried, When all above is bedlam, you'd do best to remain buried At least until uncertainty becomes a toxic dread And safety suffocates; do dare you then stick out your head?

primaryArticles.title: 9. Melissa
primaryArticles.desc: When the battles you've been fighting aren't won by strength of arms, Too much time for contemplation undermines its famous charms A head up in the clouds cannot avoid the thundershock; Though hiding helps the body, the mind could use a walk

primaryArticles.title: 10. Geneviève
primaryArticles.desc: There's a kind of camaraderie you can't find on the field But which grows in great abundance underneath an earthen shield A sort of social sorting sets the sterner set apart And allows the seeds of leadership a healthy growing start

primaryArticles.title: 11. Ilse
primaryArticles.desc: When you've left your bunker far behind to taste the summer air, There's a curious desire to reoccupy that lair With its certainty and stasis, its unchanging quantum state But there is no going home for you; the past will never wait.

primaryArticles.title: 12. Delfina
primaryArticles.desc: Though life below the trenches has a homely undertone — There's a postman and a milkman, and a bunk to call your own And your fellows will defend you, never minding what may come — You must not forget: this tunnel's where you're at, not where you're from

primaryArticles.title: 13. Nhung
primaryArticles.desc: When living in your head too long becomes an awful hassle, There's better uses for a fortified cerebral castle Like shoring up the claims your friends make on their own demesnes; But mind somatic tolls on fending other people's brains.

primaryArticles.title: 14. Flora
primaryArticles.desc: Still, there's something to be said for living large within our graves; It's a means to feel akin to our ancestors with their caves Antecedents of those troupers who before us marched to die Serving causes they believed in, never truly knowing why.

primaryArticles.title: 15. Xinyi
primaryArticles.desc: When the nature of a dug-out can't admit for lengthy stays, Though it's fit for purpose now, that's only just a passing phase If long you dwell within it, change its essence to the core, It becomes a different beast, and not a dug-out anymore.

primaryArticles.title: 16. Mali
primaryArticles.desc: In digging down beneath the slabs, disturbing ancient earth As bygone Emperors once did to bury things of worth, That in the afterlife they might retain their Earthly spoil, Remind yourself you're not the only thing beneath the soil.

primaryArticles.title: 17. Udo
primaryArticles.desc: When you're a long-term tenant, you know every glinting grain Like a practical geologist, with silt upon the brain Acreage of dirt becoming well-loved bunks and shelves, And all this filthy tackle mere extensions of our selves.

primaryArticles.title: 18. Nastya
primaryArticles.desc: If the jackboots set you running and you've got no place to turn, And you find yourself in trenches strange, it's logical to yearn For that pleasant little hidey-hole away from your new hosts; In long-abandoned dug-outs dwell their own unhappy ghosts.

primaryArticles.title: 19. Nimkii
primaryArticles.desc: When you've spent a couple lifetimes in the trenches with your mates There's a closeness beyond family, or destiny, or fate You become the kind of bosom buds that no-one can deny, In the muck you're forging friendships that on no account may die.

primaryArticles.title: 20. Eileen
primaryArticles.desc: There's a funny sort of feeling that you get below the grade It can warp your sense of purpose, cause your memories to fade A transformation gradual no soldier can resist, though It's comforting to note that what's important will persist.

primaryArticles.title: 21. Daniil
primaryArticles.desc: When you shove a bunch of people in a huddle in a hole, There's a curious division of diversity of soul And an equalizing quality to humble, filthy toil; The genius-eating tenor of democratizing soil.

primaryArticles.title: 22. Noor
primaryArticles.desc: Woe betide the quartermaster who must lord above these pits, Keeping track of all the bodies warm and all their sundry bits It's a Herculean task to bring to balance our amounts, We who march upon the margins, where it's disarray that counts.

primaryArticles.title: 23. Michael
primaryArticles.desc: When your faith is faint and foundering, and nothing's gone to plan, Yet we fallen folk in Abaddon have need of more than man, And little's gained from pleading to the powers we've outgrown, And plenty left to pray for — it's no sin to make our own.

primaryArticles.title: 24. Jennifer
primaryArticles.desc: No gap or gulf however vast cannot be bridged by love, Though stretching 'cross an ocean or the mound of soil above Yet still there's something to be said for crass proximity And all the daily debts accrued and paid by you, and me.

primaryArticles.title: 25. Howard
primaryArticles.desc: We think we know the men we are when warm beneath the sun, But some truths are deeply buried by us, each and every one We find out who our friends are when we're hard against the scrum: Not the ones ordained for action, but the ones that deign to come.

primaryArticles.title: 26. Jay
primaryArticles.desc: There are those who watch the battlements, and those who bunker down, And those who see the picture whole, who know that soon we'll drown In tears and blood we'll shed from wounds the causes of which stem From lack of visionary thought beyond just "us" and "th…

primaryArticles.title: 27. Dolores
primaryArticles.desc: When the planning meets the fighting and the planning loses out, And there's no-one left upon the field who wields sufficient clout To keep the battle rolling, or to bring it to a close Someone always takes initiative; but who? 'til then, who knows?

primaryArticles.title: 28. Eszter
primaryArticles.desc: Every acre of this sodden earth has known the tread of feet There is presence in the particles, its story incomplete Yet can those who dug before us help to further dig the hole? Does the genius of a loci have its own peculiar soul?

primaryArticles.title: 29. Amelia
primaryArticles.desc: When waiting is a habit 'neath the weighty weight of soil, Keeping time and counting moments, curling inward like a coil Tense and nervous and distracted, 'til resumption of our toil, We then spring to life so precious, and our blood is brought to boil.

primaryArticles.title: 30. Bastien
primaryArticles.desc: Underfoot and out of sight is where we make our homes, In the subterranean shadows like a pack of busy gnomes Keeping up the nerve to dwell within demands an iron will, But it helps to know that always there are deeper places still.

primaryArticles.title: 31. Wilhelmina
primaryArticles.desc: When you're underneath the cover and you're looking for your mates, When you're crawling through the muck and mud to learn their sorry fates Under rotten timbers fallen, or in craters hewn by shell, It's not easy to remember that the home front's also hell.

primaryArticles.title: 32. Polyxeni
primaryArticles.desc: Should the tally of the dead feel too profound for math to count, And the losses keep on piling to a staggering amount, Keep your focus off the rattling of the ragged spectre's chain, And your eye upon the prize: those precious bodies which remain.

primaryArticles.title: 33. Rozálie
primaryArticles.desc: When they say the danger's over but you see the sunset red, And the glow upon the gloaming fills your warning heart with dread, Look upon the faces dearest to you in that dark'ning hour — Know that they are brilliant also, gleaming with such lambent power.

The Northern Ear of the Unusual Incidents Unit searches through the lights that carry droves of ignorant tourists worldwide to the Arctic Circle. In a landscape blanketed by radar stations in the shadow of the faceoff between the Soviet Union and the United States, two dozen scientists, agents and field operatives labor in anticipation of conflicts beyond physical squabbles.

collections.description: People, like webs, are interconnected, forever intertwining and unraveling in the world around them. To the spider, the web is a source of nourishment, comfort, safety. To the fly, it is a graveyard. Much like our Earth, it is a source of prosperity and of dread. The SCP Foundation and the GOC, once forces to be reckoned with, are now shells of their former selves. These organizations have been forced even further into the shadows by emerging powers, namely, the national organizations of the world, maintaining both their national interests and the veil itself. However, like the empires of old, they refuse to go gently. Despite their diminished state, the Foundation and the Coalition continue in their eternal struggle to abide by their mission statements, clawing their way into every facet of our modern world.

collections.description: Our Engine writhes in misery at the unnatural abuse allowed to persist by our enemies. The Foundation feigns ignorance, yet their trespasses have never been more clear. So wicked they are, as the day we first understood them — an organisation of sycophants who thrive in their own arrogant malfeasance, casting blame to those without and never within. Their spirits shall falter due to a wound which they cannot hide. Soon the rest of our world shall flock upon them like feasting carrion birds . We will be there once the final bones are picked clean. But until then, we must learn the extent of their narcissistic ignorance. Our preparations begin, and our patience shall be rewarded. Heed the Engine’s will. Listen to its eternal hum and follow in its Steps.

collections.description: When the sun goes down, humanity is alone to face abnormal phenomena. They appear only at night, for everyone to see, and exist solely to terrify the humans, at best. At worst, to kill or torture them. Those who go out at night sometimes don't come back. Those who drive at night sometimes have accidents. Even the comfort of the bedroom sometimes isn't safe. However, as soon as the night is over and the sun rises at the horizon, the anomalies disappear, along with everyone's memories of it. All of humanity forgets what they were terrified of. Deaths become disappearances or miscellaneous news. Every memory of these terrifying nights only stays as a nightmare fading as time goes on, and everyone resumes their daily lives.

collections.description: The canon "Cyców's Hell" focuses on the existence of a demonic layer of reality that is separated from us by a barrier. It just so happens that this barrier is the thinnest in the inconspicuous Cyców gmina. Due to the anomalies occurring there, the Foundation quickly secures the area of the entire commune, later naming it Nx-79 "Gmina Cyców", completely cutting it off from the rest of the civilization. Site PL-79 is built to oversee the entire area of the Nexus and to investigate anomalies related to the demonic layer of reality. It turns out, however, that the Foundation is not the only organization that knows about its existence. In the forest located in the village of Cyców, there are armaments plants belonging to Hunter Industries, as well as their headquarters. collections.description: The world is a weird and wonderful place. Though my stay here was short, I could not have picked a better place to be. The earth, with its cultures, its peoples, its oceans, its continents. Its forests. Its deserts. Its tundras. The earth, where you can fly around the globe in two days. The universe, where stars and planets circle around us, or we circle them; sometimes it's hard to tell. I've met many on my journey. I feel blessed for each and every one of them. primaryArticles.title: Maim the Sky, Slay the Sun

collections.description: The sky darkened. The world died. Humanity burrowed. The sky cleared. The world bloomed. Humanity festered. Things are greater now. Taller. Deeper. Made to weather the longest eons. They're worse now. Deeper. Lonelier. Full of sludge, and muck, and scum. Things are different, but history has a way of clawing its way back from the darkest boundaries. Old forces persist. Old enemies remain. Most of all, old grudges tug away at distant generations, and what an incessant pull they have. Flea is a child of a storied family. Years ago, she fled to a storied city. She's built up her own grudges since, stealing things and swindling people, but they're nothing compared to what has persisted beyond the clouds' vanished veil.

collections.description: I had a bit of trouble coming up with a decent name for this hub. Multiple people suggested something to the effect of 'all that glitters', but that seemed a little too trite. So I was looking up quotes from the Merchant of Venice, hoping something there might be appropriate, and lo and behold I see that the original Shakespeare quote is in fact "All that glisters is not gold". It carries the same meaning, but the obsolete Elizabethan synonym gives it a veneer of antiquity and pretentiousness that I feel is appropriate with this series.

This may or may not also entail an "SK-Class Dominance Shift", depending on the power and resources available to newly animated things. An MA-Class Mass Animation Scenario should not be declared until at least one of the following is affirmed: Return of the situation to normalcy, i.e. deactivating the newly animated entities and erasing memories of the event, is infeasible. Location and destruction of the affected things is considered impractical or unethical.

primaryArticles.desc: Decibelles

collections.description: And here it is; the revelation. Just as there's no real differences between myself and I, there's truly no differences between acceptance and denial. The only two things defining each are semantics and level of emotions. Maybe that's why I had trouble understanding the differences, how to apply them to myself; it's all a matter of shifting perspective. Maybe there's an end in sight. A goalpost where I can break free of the consistent years spent in nothingness, feeling my atoms turn to wet, and resisting. All I have to do is step forward, remember that "yes" is "yes", and hold on. Eventually, the answer will come for why things are the way they are. Answers always come.

It depicted a young man with a meticulously trimmed beard dressed in a ragged flannel, his arm around an even younger man with dark green eyes, and long black hair tied back in a ponytail. The men in the photo had ear to ear grins. Their troubles had not yet come to pass. He then turned to the elderly woman sitting next to him at the table who looked at him with a kind, sympathetic smile. "I have never doubted anything more in my life, 45," he said with a sad grin. "Phineas," the old woman said softly, "Vince tried to kill you. The kind young man you knew has finally died. What stands in his place is nothing short of a monster."
